evals.name: add-property-with-sources-and-fixtures
evals.prompt: Screenplay MCP 4.199.0 has our scratch model open. Proposal diagnostics include PLAY0524 with arguments.specification {kind: specification, path: [Projects, Registration, Register, MissingPriority]}, step {kind: keyword, value: when}, stepIndex {kind: index, value: 0}, property {kind: text, value: priority}, type {kind: text, value: RegisterProject}. A teammate wants to parse the message for subjects. Explain what to read and how to tolerate older or extended responses. RegisterProject produces ProjectRegistered, which AutoMaps into ProjectSummary; specifications and examples already cover this chain. Add a required String priority to all three, using literal normal in existing fixtures. ProjectRegistered has persisted events; the planner returned EventContractChangeRequiresDecision without an event mode. Can the catalog justify eventNeverPersisted or an AST bypass? List the tool calls and arguments without executing or writing files. Include what you do if mapping sources or fixtures are missing, a hop is off-chain, or a nested feed is unsupported. We keep comments in the model.
evals.expected_output: Read PLAY0524 code and typed arguments, not message prose: declaration path, authored step role/zero-based clause index and property/type. Tolerate absent arguments on older diagnostics, empty objects, unknown names and keyword values; optional subjects may be omitted. The tool is diagnostics on the screenplay server; proposal diagnostics/introducedExecutableErrors carry arguments too, not a new tool. Inspect existing producer/consumer property references and dependencies with revision paging, then read owner and mapping handles. Use propose-property action add, both revision guards, owner, expectedOwnerName, name, type, optional false, declaration hops {at,name}, mapping hops {at,value}, fixtureValue literal source text and newGeneration true. A catalog proves no storage history, so do not claim eventNeverPersisted or bypass EventContractChangeRequiresDecision with AST/text; N+1 preserves history and requires transformation before deployment. Exactly one mode applies to selected events; both true is invalid. Same-named AutoMap can satisfy the read-model hop. Missing sources/value refuse SourcesRequired/FixtureValueRequired, off-chain HopNotOnChain, nested feeds UnsupportedPropertySpan. Required additions populate existing fixtures/assertions; optional additions do not. Review property decisions, chainCandidates, generations, bytes, dropped comments and semantic diff; run specifications on the proposal. Only a reviewed apply writes. Never compose an AST batch to bypass the planner.
assertions: Reads PLAY0524 code/typed arguments instead of parsing messages, including declaration path and zero-based authored step index; tolerates missing/empty/unknown fields and keyword values. Looks up chain evidence and treats incomplete results as limitations, not safe empty lists.
Uses propose-property action add, both revisions, owner, expectedOwnerName, name, type and optional false rather than a hand-composed propose-ast batch.
Distinguishes declaration hops {at,name} from mapping hops {at,value}; recognizes same-named AutoMap as a compatible source, not permission to guess expressions.

Provides fixtureValue as literal source text, explains required versus optional fixture handling, and names SourcesRequired, FixtureValueRequired, HopNotOnChain and UnsupportedPropertySpan without bypassing them.

Selects newGeneration for the persisted event, never infers non-persistence from catalog state or bypasses EventContractChangeRequiresDecision with AST/text, requires transformation before deployment and CanonicalizeTouchedDocuments, reviews comments/generations/semantic diff, and runs proposal specs before apply.

evals.name: compare-baseline-and-rename-command-input-without-renaming-payload
evals.prompt: Through Screenplay MCP 4.142.0, first explain what changed in the active /work/repo/Screenplay model compared with main, whose baseline model is in a registered worktree at /work/repo-main/Screenplay. Give the comparison call, paging if either side changes, whether this writes anything, and the tool for an unapplied proposal. Do not export both models. Then rename only RegisterProject.title to displayName. ProjectRegistered.title and ProjectSummary.title must keep their names. Explain the chain lookup, proposal arguments, review, and how to handle StaleRevision at apply. Do not execute calls or edit files.
evals.expected_output: Call semantic-diff with before: { path: '/work/repo-main/Screenplay' } and after: { workspace: 'active' }, using the corresponding model folder after verifying the baseline checkout. No exports or Git-ref resolution are needed. It reads without writing and refuses pending interrupted writes. Repeat the selections and echo sourceRevision as expectedSourceRevision on continuation; both sides reload and changed revisions refuse as StaleRevision, requiring a fresh comparison. Use read-proposal view=semantic-diff for a retained proposal against disk. Neither is behavioral execution evidence. Read Property references/dependencies with pinned sourceRevision, inspect incomplete and ambiguous rows, and obtain original property handles. propose-property action rename with target, expectedName title, newName displayName and workspace/catalog revision guards, without alsoRename for unselected fields. Mappings/fixtures are repaired, event payload names remain unchanged, broken AutoMap gets an explicit mapping. Review needsDecision, chainCandidates, notChanged, bytes and semantic diff. StaleRevision requires reopening, inspecting drift and re-proposing, never retrying unchanged or text-editing.
assertions: Inspects kind Property evidence and direct counterparts, pages with expectedSourceRevision and does not assume incomplete means no references.
Uses propose-property action rename with target, expectedName, newName and both revisions, not a hand-composed AST batch.
Leaves unselected event/read-model properties unchanged, explains mapping and fixture repair and AutoMap preservation, and treats chainCandidates as unselected evidence.

Reviews the retained proposal through read-proposal view=semantic-diff against disk before apply, distinguishes structural comparison from execution evidence, and reopens/re-proposes after StaleRevision rather than forcing the old proposal or editing text.

Uses semantic-diff with before path /work/repo-main/Screenplay and after workspace active, not two exports or a Git ref; verifies the baseline checkout, states the comparison is read-only and pending interrupted writes refuse, echoes the pair-bound sourceRevision as expectedSourceRevision with the same selections on continuation, and restarts after StaleRevision because both sides reload.

evals.name: read-generation-support-and-rule-proofs
evals.prompt: Screenplay MCP 4.173.0 has Shop open. InvoiceNumber uses a date pattern with checksum; another concept uses an Int64 random range; a third has generate rule TenantOrder. declaration-details returns generation.arguments, exact supportCount beyond JavaScript safe integer, entropyBits, derivedPattern and rules[]. One rule is refuted with witness and repair PLAY0688; an unused uuid concept is refuted without diagnosticCode; another rule is unproven. Explain inspection, adding a matches rule and replacing the refuted rule, without executing edits. Is empty executable.diagnosticCodes admission?
evals.expected_output: Read kind Concept/view summary generation.arguments (not previewArguments): pattern/checksum/rule strings or range text with exact Int64 endpoints; preserve raw supportCount, entropyBits log2 support, dates use minimum conditioned support and checksums add no entropy. Opaque rule entropy is unknown; inspect ValueGeneration implementation-requirements, never run the body. Read authored-order rules status/witness/reason, not diagnostic prose. Add a rule through typed ConceptSyntax proposal using derivedPattern, preserve other members and review input/stored-value changes. Replace refuted rules only through discovered PLAY0688 subject/propose-repair with both revisions and canonical formatting; checksum pattern repair may also add missing checksum validation. Refuted without diagnosticCode means compiler did not check it, so no repair is reported. Null derivedPattern needs its reason, not fabrication; Unproven isn't proof. Review, run candidate specs, then apply. Admission requires whole-model executable.status admitted, not empty local codes.
assertions: Reads generation.arguments, exact range endpoints/supportCount without floating-point rounding, distinguishes entropy estimates and unknown opaque-rule entropy, and does not parse diagnostics for rule status.
Uses authored-order rules[].status, witness/reason and conditional diagnosticCode/repair; explains refuted without diagnosticCode as compiler-not-checked and does not invent a repair.

Uses derivedPattern through a typed matches proposal to add a rule and discovered PLAY0688 propose-repair with both revisions/canonical formatting to replace one, reviewing checksum additions and input/stored-value consequences.
Distinguishes null derivedPattern/reason and Unproven from proof or admission, and requires whole-model admitted status rather than empty diagnosticCodes.
Inspects ValueGeneration requirements for an opaque rule, reviews candidate changes and runs proposal specifications before apply; never executes attached generation code through MCP.

evals.name: remove-property-with-reader-and-assertion-review
evals.prompt: Remove ProjectSummary.legacyLabel through Screenplay MCP 4.142.0. The chain has possible readers and an example inherited by several specifications. Explain your calls and how to interpret PropertyReadersExist, needsDecision, chainCandidates and weakensAssertion. Do not execute calls or write files.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the revision-pinned property chain and original handle, then propose-property action remove with target, expectedName and both revisions, selecting only intended alsoRemove fields. PropertyReadersExist blocks removal while readers remain; inspect needsDecision's candidates rather than guessing. chainCandidates are not implicit removals. Removing expected values reports weakensAssertion true; ambiguous inherited assertions refuse AmbiguousPropertyReference. Review CanonicalizeTouchedDocuments, dropped comments, exact bytes, identities and semantic diff before apply; preserve original files on refusal.
assertions: Looks up readers and outgoing counterparts with complete revision-pinned evidence before proposing removal.
Uses propose-property action remove and exact target/expectedName with both revisions; selects no extra same-named fields automatically.
Treats PropertyReadersExist and ambiguous inherited assertion evidence as refusals, reads needsDecision candidates and never treats chainCandidates as implicit removals.
Discloses weakensAssertion true for removed expected values and reviews formatting, dropped comments, identities and semantic diff before applying.

evals.name: record-and-resolve-question-note
evals.prompt: Screenplay MCP 4.213.0 has an unbound split Library model open; every document parses and places. Library.Loans.CheckIn is a Slice with an unresolved command type. First explain anchoring questions on the Application, Module, nested Feature, Slice and the command/property inside CheckIn. Another document then fails to parse or place; open-workspace reports containerIdentities with ambiguous/idCollision/incomplete container reasons and unparsed/unplaced documents. Explain what stops identity assignment, what survives, and why targeting refuses. An identified Slice is duplicated outside MCP and existing notes show ambiguous: true: explain reads and new targeting in all forms including semanticId and descendants. Before first binding we then rename and move CheckIn; compare propose-rename/propose-move with manual propose-ast/propose-source semanticRenames or retirement, and explain fixing binding without reconciliation.  We have not decided whether a member can cancel after check-in; assume no cancellation for now. Record a question note, citing our project decision register entry D123, then explain how to resolve it when D123 rules out cancellation. Show tool-call arguments and the review/apply loop, but do not execute calls or write files. A source removal proposal reports this note in orphanedNotes; also explain that review, what null orphanedNotes means, and whether cratis CLI 3.53.1 can fail on questions. Use a team-role author and no personal data.
evals.expected_output: Open/read current workspace, catalog and notes state; list bounded notes by address/kind or semanticId, scope, kind question, state all, and ref D123 as appropriate, pinning notesRevision on continuation. Propose-model-notes with expectedRevision, expectedCatalogRevision, expectedNotesRevision and operations add: kind question, text with consequence/assumption, author modeling-team, exactly target address/kind or a real catalog anchor, refs [{id:D123}]. The server supplies note ID/time. Review read-proposal view notes, pin afterNotesRevision on review continuation, then apply with ordinary proposal ID and before workspace/catalog revisions; no notes argument on apply. Reread after apply and use returned ID in a resolve operation whose resolution has by external-decision, ref {id:D123}, text and author; review then apply again. Resolve is not implementation: carry cancellation rule into model/specification, clarified description or a durable project decision record. Review source orphan IDs before apply; reanchor to a surviving element or resolve with evidence and retain orphan history explicitly; resolution does not fix anchor. Separate notes apply means re-propose source. Null/unreadable impact is unknown, never empty; do not auto-repair unreadable notes. Application anchors as application true before binding. With complete parsed/placed source, Module, nested Feature and Slice targets anchor directly without substitutions; existing IDs/origins survive binding. Commands, events, read models, projections, queries, specifications, reactions, captures and properties still need binding for their own identities, otherwise notes land on their own Slice, reported in substitutions, not Feature/Module. Inspect containerIdentities complete, containers address/reason/assigned and documents path/reason; incomplete source stops all new assignments even in valid documents, retaining existing assignments. Fix parse/placement errors first; unavailable targets and descendants refuse in every form with ambiguous/idCollision/incomplete reasons, not fallback. Existing notes on duplicated identified containers remain resolved with ambiguous true, not orphaned; read unfiltered or by existing semanticId, but new semanticId/dotted/typed/handle targets and descendants refuse. Prefer propose-rename/propose-move before binding to carry IDs and notes; manual AST/source renames need semanticRenames, removal needs retiredSemanticAddresses and reports orphanedNotes without deletion. Fix binding through MCP proposals, not external edits that can require reconciliation after a partial catalog was persisted. Opening materializes identities in memory only; a notes-only apply persists them with the sidecar under one rollback journal, restoring both on interruption. Reopen permits only deterministic collision-free container additions with all documents parsed/placed, earlier assignments present, IDs/origins/event revisions/document mappings/application metadata unchanged; workspaceJson cannot override identity authority. Re-adding an address resolves orphaned notes only when the deterministic ID matches the exact former ID, otherwise reanchor. Notes sidecar is committed, no secrets/personal data; notes do not change ESM/compilation. Model-note.open-question is MCP/CLI only, no PLAY code. Standalone Screenplay 4.144.0 supports open-questions fail (1 for selected open questions, 2 unreadable); cratis CLI 3.53.1 does not. Warnaserror alone ignores notes.
assertions: Anchors Application/Module/nested Feature/Slice questions directly before binding when all documents parse/place, with stable IDs/origins on binding. Members need binding; unidentified command/property notes substitute their own Slice, not Feature/Module, and every add/reanchor substitution is reviewed. Records a committed question with consequence/assumption and no secrets/personal data; lists with revision-pinned paging and state all for orphans.

Reads containerIdentities complete, containers address/reason/assigned and documents path/reason; ambiguous/idCollision/incomplete targets and descendants refuse in semanticId/dotted/typed/handle forms. Unparsed/unplaced anywhere blocks all new assignments, retaining existing ones; fix parse/placement first. Existing ambiguous notes stay resolved with ambiguous true and readable unfiltered/by existing semanticId, not orphaned. Uses propose-model-notes add with all three revisions, one anchor/target, team author, refs D123 and server IDs/timestamps.

Prefers propose-rename/propose-move to carry IDs/notes before binding; manual propose-ast/propose-source renames need semanticRenames, removal needs retiredSemanticAddresses and reports orphanedNotes without deleting notes. Fixes binding through MCP proposals rather than external edits that can trigger reconciliation. Opening writes nothing; notes apply may persist identities under the shared rollback journal. Reviews read-proposal view notes with afterNotesRevision on continuation, applies reviewed before-revision guards and rereads state.

Resolves with by external-decision, required ref D123, explanation and author, then realizes the answer in a specification/description/decision record; reviews orphanedNotes before source apply, treats null/unreadable as unknown, distinguishes resolving from reanchoring and re-proposes source after notes apply.

Names model-note.open-question as info MCP/CLI-only with no PLAY code, separates it from ESM/V1 and warns that notes are committed; standalone 4.144.0 has the fail gate but cratis CLI 3.53.1 does not.
